e-03.title: Decide wetin to ask before you reply
e-03.goal: Decide which information you really need before replying invitation text, and write short English reply to ask for am.
e-03.material:
You get text from your friend Ari. ‘Make we play soccer tomorrow!’
You think say e sound good, but dis text alone no give you enough information to decide whether you fit go.
e-03.thinking.1: Choose di questions wey you need
e-03.thinking.2: Write reply wey get questions inside
e-03.s.s1.prompt: Choose everything wey you must know before you fit answer, ‘I can go.’
e-03.s.s1.hint.0: Check whether di answer to each question don already dey for di text.
e-03.s.s1.hint.1: Try each question one by one: if you no get di answer, you fit talk ‘I’ll come’?
e-03.s.s1.r.a: You need di time. But with only this, you no know where to go. Check whether you need anything else.
e-03.s.s1.r.b: You need di place. But with only this, you no know wetin time e be. Check whether you need anything else.
e-03.s.s1.r.c: Ball go nice to get, but you no need am to decide whether you fit go.
e-03.s.s1.r.d: E fit help, but you fit decide whether you go without am. Think whether na really necessary information.
e-03.s.s1.r.e: Ari don already talk make we play soccer. This question dey ask about something wey you don know already.
e-03.s.s1.r.f: E good to know di reason because curiosity, but you no need am to decide whether you fit go. Question no become necessary just because e start with question word.
e-03.s.s1.explain: If you no know di time and place, you no fit decide whether e fit your schedule or whether you fit reach there. If you choose only one, test am again: without di other one, you fit talk ‘I’ll come’? (If you know only di time, you no know where to go; if you know only di place, you no know wetin time.)
e-03.s.s1.acc.0: E natural to want know who else dey come too. But di main point na say you no fit answer without di time and place.
e-03.s.s2.prompt: Write reply to Ari for English. Show say you wan join, and include question to ask for di information wey you choose above.
e-03.s.s2.hint.0: First, write short phrase wey mean ‘Sounds good!’
e-03.s.s2.hint.1: You fit join di two questions wey you choose into one sentence too.
e-03.s.s2.selfAssess.0: After Ari read my reply, e fit tell me di time and place?
e-03.s.s2.selfAssess.1: E get both friendly reply and di questions?
e-03.s.s2.modelNote.1: I ask am with longer sentence.

e-09.title: Before you answer your junior ‘Could you look at it at some point?’
e-09.goal: Pick out di information wey vague request leave out, and write English reply wey politely ask di questions you need.
e-09.material:
You get message from student one class below you. You hardly know each other.

‘Hi! Sorry to bother you, but could you look at my essay at some point? Thanks!!’

You wan help, but you busy this week.
e-09.thinking.1: Choose which questions you need first
e-09.s.s1.prompt: Choose everything wey you need to know before replying, so you fit decide whether you fit help and how to help well.
e-09.s.s1.hint.0: Underline di vague words for di message, and write one line each to explain why each word make your decision hard.
e-09.s.s1.hint.1: Try each question one by one: if e no get answer, you fit talk ‘Yes, I’ll do it’?
e-09.s.s1.r.a: You need di deadline. But from this alone, you no know wetin kind of help dem need. Check whether you need another question.
e-09.s.s1.r.b: You need know di kind of help. But from this alone, you no know by when dem need am. Check whether you need another question.
e-09.s.s1.r.c: You need di length to estimate how much time e go take. Check whether you need other questions too.
e-09.s.s1.r.d: Last year grades no relate directly to whether or how you fit help with this essay.
e-09.s.s1.r.e: Whether dem get another person to help no change whether or how you fit help.
e-09.s.s1.explain: ‘At some point’ no clear about when, and ‘look at’ no clear about di kind of help. You need deadline, di help dem want, and di length to decide whether you fit make time. If you choose only some, test whether you fit help without answer to any question wey you leave out.
e-09.s.s1.acc.0: Deadline and di kind of help dem want na di main points, and you go learn di length after dem send am, so e make sense to leave that one out.
e-09.s.s1.acc.1: E also make sense to first use deadline and length to decide whether you fit make time, then ask about di kind of help later.
e-09.s.s1.acc.2: Even though you busy this week, you fit first estimate whether you fit help from di kind of help dem need and di length. But you go need know di deadline soon.
e-09.s.s2.prompt: Write reply to your junior for English. Politely show say you ready to help, and include at least two questions wey you choose above.
e-09.s.s2.hint.0: Choose two questions wey go affect whether you fit help, or how you go help.
e-09.s.s2.hint.1: Write one question for each sentence, and put phrase about helping right at di start.
e-09.s.s2.placeholder: Example: Sure, I'd be happy to help! ...
e-09.s.s2.selfAssess.0: After reading my reply, your junior fit tell me di deadline and di help wey dem want?
e-09.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You fit see both say you wan help and di questions?
e-09.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Di tone fit person wey you hardly know?

e-10.title: Polite refusal, or e still get chance?
e-10.goal: As dem show each sentence of polite email, change your judgment about wetin di other person really mean, then write suitable reply.
e-10.material: You send proposal to Ms. Rowe, wey dey in charge for school, to make school vegetable garden. Di reply email dey show one sentence at a time.
e-10.thinking.0: Guess di intention behind polite tone
e-10.thinking.1: Change your judgment when new information come
e-10.prereq.1: Basic understanding of polite refusal expressions
e-10.s.s1.prompt: Read di email one part at a time, and each time choose whether you think dem go accept di proposal.
e-10.s.s1.hint.0: First decide whether di new sentence change di meaning of di earlier one or continue am.
e-10.s.s1.hint.1: Mark words wey change di direction (But) and specific words like dates and purposes.
e-10.s.s1.st.0.ask: From this sentence alone, wetin be di most reasonable judgment?
e-10.s.s1.st.0.after: Praise alone no show di decision. E fit be start of gentle refusal or just greeting. Di next sentence matter.
e-10.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Dem likely go approve am, and she go let us know soon.
e-10.s.s1.st.0.r.a: ‘Interesting’ na praise, but e no be word for decision or approval.
e-10.s.s1.st.0.o.b: She fit dey plan to refuse politely.
e-10.s.s1.st.0.o.c: We no fit know di decision yet; we need see di next sentence.
e-10.s.s1.st.1.after: Di time range ‘this year’ matter. If you read am as ‘polite refusal’ for di first step, this sentence support that reading, but e no mean permanent refusal yet.
e-10.s.s1.st.1.o.a: E talk say this year go hard, and e never talk anything about after that.
e-10.s.s1.st.1.o.b: E mean complete refusal from now on, no matter wetin happen this year.
e-10.s.s1.st.1.r.b: E only talk ‘this year budget.’ E never talk say na permanent refusal.
e-10.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Na only budget problem, so dem go solve am soon and we fit start this year.
e-10.s.s1.st.1.r.c: E talk say dem don already set di budget.
e-10.s.s1.st.2.ask: Read reach di last sentence and judge again.
e-10.s.s1.st.2.after: Di direction change with ‘But,’ and di deadline (Friday), purpose (director), and time (March) clear. Whether you read am as not decided yet or intention to move forward, if you don firmly decide ‘polite refusal’ before, you need change your judgment.
e-10.s.s1.st.2.o.a: Na just courtesy, so you no need reply.
e-10.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Person wey only wan refuse no go give deadline (Friday) and purpose (director, March) with detail.
e-10.s.s1.st.2.o.b: She never decide whether to refuse yet; she dey gather information to judge.
e-10.s.s1.st.2.r.b: This reading fit work too. But ‘I will show it to the director before the March budget meeting’ sound more like she wan move forward.
e-10.s.s1.st.2.o.c: She interested, and she dey ask for materials so dem fit move am forward at March budget meeting.
e-10.s.s1.reflect: Explain how your judgment change for third step after you judge ‘difficult’ for second step. Which words (But, by Friday, before ... March) cause the change?
e-10.s.s2.prompt: Write how your judgment for first step different from your last (third) step, and which expressions make am different. You fit write Korean or English. (If e no change, explain why e stay the same.)
e-10.s.s2.hint.0: First, write the choice wey you make for step 1 in one sentence.
e-10.s.s2.hint.1: From expressions wey newly show for step 3 (But, Friday, March, etc.), choose one wey change your judgment.
e-10.s.s2.placeholder: Example: At first I thought ... but because of ...
e-10.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You clearly write di judgment wey you choose first?
e-10.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You pick out and write which expression from di email change your judgment?
e-10.s.s2.selfAssess.2: If e no change, you explain why using clues from di email?
e-10.s.s2.model.0: At first I think say na polite refusal, but for di last sentence I see say after ‘But’ she ask for estimate by Friday, so I change my mind and think say she interested.
e-10.s.s3.prompt: Write reply to Ms. Rowe for English. Show thanks and say you understand di situation, and promise to send wetin she ask for by di requested day (Friday).
e-10.s.s3.hint.0: Read again wetin di last sentence for di email ask for (wetin and by when) and put those details in your answer just as dem be.
e-10.s.s3.hint.1: Try write am in this order: one sentence to thank am, one sentence to show understanding, one sentence with your promise.
e-10.s.s3.placeholder: Example: Thank you for your reply. ...
e-10.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Your reply answer exactly wetin Ms. Rowe ask for last?
e-10.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You use expression to show say you understand this year budget no allow am?
e-10.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You avoid showing too much disappointment?
e-10.s.s3.modelNote.1: Answer wey suggest changing di plan.

e-01.title: Join two lines for library notice to check Ben plan
e-01.goal: Join two different lines for di notice (normal timetable and this week own exception), decide for each day whether your friend plan go work, and tell am for English.
e-01.material:
Di notice wey dey for school library door (na words only, no picture):

Library
Open: Mon, Wed, Fri  3:00-4:00
This week: closed on Friday (cleaning day).

Your friend Ben talk say, ‘Make we go library on Thursday and Friday this week!’
e-01.thinking.0: Use several lines for notice to make decision
e-01.thinking.1: Find separate proof for each day
e-01.thinking.2: Check your friend plan against di proof
e-01.s.s1.prompt: Ben fit use di library on both Thursday and Friday this week, as e plan?
e-01.s.s1.hint.0: Check Thursday and Friday one by one, and compare wetin each line for di notice talk about di day.
e-01.s.s1.hint.1: Check whether di ‘Open’ line and di ‘This week’ line get different work.
e-01.s.s1.r.a: You fit never read both lines for di notice. Check whether Thursday dey among di days wey open, and whether dem add special note about Friday.
e-01.s.s1.r.c: Library dey open on Friday normally, but di ‘This week’ line talk something different about this week.
e-01.s.s1.r.d: Check again whether Thursday dey for di list of days wey open (Open).
e-01.s.s1.explain: Thursday no dey among di days wey open (Mon, Wed, Fri), and although Friday dey open normally, this week e say ‘closed on Friday.’ So none of di two days go work.
e-01.s.s2.prompt: Choose every line wey you need to judge Ben plan (Thursday and Friday).
e-01.s.s2.hint.0: Try remove each line and see whether e go harder to judge Thursday or Friday.
e-01.s.s2.hint.1: Keep wetin Ben talk separate from di lines for di notice.
e-01.s.s2.r.a: You need this to judge Thursday, but this line alone no tell you about Friday for this week (library dey open normally). Check whether you need another line too.
e-01.s.s2.r.b: You need this to judge Friday, but this line no talk anything about Thursday. Find which line go let you judge Thursday.
e-01.s.s2.r.c: Na title only, so e no get information about days.
e-01.s.s2.r.d: Na Ben suggestion. Suggestion na something wey you suppose check, no be proof.
e-01.s.s2.explain: Di Open line show say Thursday no be day wey library open, and di This week line show say library close on Friday this week. Either one alone no fit help you judge both days. If you choose only one, check which day remain.
e-01.s.s3.prompt: Reply Ben for English with one or two sentences. Give reason why una no fit go on Thursday and reason why una no fit go on Friday.
e-01.s.s3.hint.0: First, write one sentence to tell Ben, ‘No, we no fit go.’
e-01.s.s3.hint.1: Write one sentence for di Thursday reason and one for di Friday reason, and connect each one to line for di notice.
e-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You give reason for Thursday and reason for Friday?
e-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You fit talk which line for di notice each reason come from?
e-01.s.s3.selfAssess.2: If you suggest another day, you check say na day wey library really dey open? (optional)

e-02.title: Find di confusing sentence for invitation message
e-02.goal: Find two sentences for short invitation message wey no match, then rewrite dem so friends no go confuse.
e-02.material: Na message wey Jun send to im classmates. (Na words only. Each line get number.)
e-02.thinking.0: Find information wey contradict each other between sentences
e-02.thinking.1: Predict di problem and rewrite am
e-02.prereq.1: Simple verbs like come / start di game
e-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose one sentence wey fit confuse friends. Na line wey no match another line.
e-02.s.s1.hint.0: Collect only di lines wey get numbers (times).
e-02.s.s1.hint.1: Compare di ‘arrival time’ and di ‘start time.’ Which one come first?
e-02.s.s1.explain: E tell people make dem come by 10, but e talk say di game go start by 9:30. You fit change line 3 or line 4. Line 1 (di park on Sunday) and line 2 (where di park dey) no clash with any other line. If you compare di lines wey get numbers (times), you go see di problem.
e-02.s.s2.prompt: Wetin fit happen if dem send dis message as e be?
e-02.s.s2.hint.0: Imagine say friend wey receive di message look di clock and do exactly wetin e talk.
e-02.s.s2.hint.1: Compare: game don start before di friend reach?
e-02.s.s2.o.a: Friend wey come by 10 go miss game wey don already start.
e-02.s.s2.o.b: Friend wey come by 9:30 go wait for empty park before di game start.
e-02.s.s2.r.b: Dis fit really happen to friend wey believe say game start by 9:30 and reach by then. But di most direct problem wey ‘come by 10’ cause na a.
e-02.s.s2.o.c: Friends end up coming on Saturday instead of Sunday.
e-02.s.s2.r.c: Di day clear say na Sunday. Di problem na di time.
e-02.s.s2.explain: Di problem depend on which time you follow. If you follow 10, you go miss di game (a); if you follow 9:30, di other line go confuse you because e talk different time (b). Either way, e happen because di two times no match.
e-02.s.s2.acc.0: Friend wey believe say game start by 9:30 and reach then to wait na real result of di clash too. a na for friend wey follow ‘10,’ and b na for friend wey follow ‘9:30.’
e-02.s.s3.prompt: Rewrite di two sentences (arrival time and game start time) for English so di times go match.
e-02.s.s3.hint.0: You fit change only one of di two times. First decide which one to change.
e-02.s.s3.hint.1: Put di arrival time before di start time, and write both times as numbers side by side to compare dem.
e-02.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Of di two times wey you write, which one earlier? Di arrival time come first?
e-02.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You picture how friend go act after reading dis message?
e-02.s.s3.modelNote.0: I make di arrival time earlier.
e-02.s.s3.modelNote.1: I make di start time later.

e-04.title: Wetin Jun want? Change your guess as dem add clues
e-04.goal: Each time dem add clue to di conversation, guess again wetin di speaker want, and explain how your guess change.
e-04.material: Jun dey talk with im mama for house. Dem go show wetin e talk small small, one piece at a time.
e-04.thinking.0: Guess di meaning wey words hide
e-04.thinking.1: Change your judgment when new information show
e-04.prereq.0: Simple words like small, hurt, closed
e-04.s.s1.prompt: Read wetin Jun talk one piece at a time, and each time guess wetin e want.
e-04.s.s1.hint.0: Find one new word for this part.
e-04.s.s1.hint.1: Check one by one whether your earlier guess match di new clue.
e-04.s.s1.st.0.ask: From this sentence alone, wetin be di most reasonable guess about wetin Jun want from im mama?
e-04.s.s1.st.0.after: You no fit know for sure from one sentence. E fit want new shoes, or e fit just dey state fact.
e-04.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Nothing for di clues don talk about P.E. class or avoiding am yet.
e-04.s.s1.st.0.o.b: E dey hope say im mama go buy new shoes for am.
e-04.s.s1.st.0.o.c: E fit just dey talk say im shoes too small.
e-04.s.s1.st.1.info: Jun: ‘Dem dey hurt me when I run. We get P.E. (physical education) class tomorrow.’
e-04.s.s1.st.1.ask: Read the new clue and guess again wetin Jun want.
e-04.s.s1.st.1.after: “It hurts” and “P.E. tomorrow” together make am clear say e want solve am before P.E. class tomorrow. If your first guess na say e just dey state fact, you need change your guess now.
e-04.s.s1.st.1.o.a: E want fix am so him feet no go pain before P.E. tomorrow.
e-04.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Again, e just dey state fact.
e-04.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Saying him feet dey pain and P.E. dey tomorrow na clue say e want solve am. That guess fit at first, but now e no fit the clues.
e-04.s.s1.st.1.r.c: E never say e wan skip. Reading am as looking for solution from “it hurts” and “P.E. tomorrow” fit the clues pass.
e-04.s.s1.st.2.ask: Read the last clue and guess wetin Jun go do.
e-04.s.s1.st.2.after: Store close today, so “buy new shoes today” no possible. Plans like going another store or talking about friend shoes both fit new clue. If na only new shoes come your mind, change plan from buying dem today.
e-04.s.s1.st.2.o.a: E go store today buy new shoes.
e-04.s.s1.st.2.r.a: This no fit clue say store close today.
e-04.s.s1.st.2.o.b: E ask him mama make she take am go another store early tomorrow morning.
e-04.s.s1.st.2.r.b: This plan fit too. But the idea Jun really mention for the end concern friend.
e-04.s.s1.st.2.o.c: E think about borrowing shoes from friend wey get same foot size.
e-04.s.s1.reflect: Your guess change for each step? If e change, name one sentence wey cause am.
e-04.s.s2.prompt: Which clue make Jun wish change from “just talking” to “solve am by tomorrow”?
e-04.s.s2.hint.0: Read the three clues in order and find when the number of possible guesses first reduce.
e-04.s.s2.hint.1: Read am with each clue removed and test whether the meaning “e want fix am” still dey.
e-04.s.s2.r.b: This sentence dey from the beginning, and alone e allow different guesses.
e-04.s.s2.r.c: This clue block one way to solve am (the store), but earlier clues don already show the wish to solve am.
e-04.s.s2.explain: “It hurts” and “P.E. tomorrow” create problem with deadline, so e read like Jun want solve am.

e-05.title: Tell different people about the same situation
e-05.goal: Write English about the same situation (missing club because of dentist appointment) to teacher and friend, with tone and length wey fit each one.
e-05.material: English club dey today at 3:30, but you get dentist appointment same time, so you no fit go. You need send message to club teacher, Ms. Han, and short text to friend for same club.
e-05.thinking.0: Compare and choose expressions according to person and situation.
e-05.thinking.1: Write am to meet politeness and length conditions.
e-05.prereq.0: Polite expressions like could / would / please
e-05.s.s1.prompt: Which message best to send to Ms. Han? (You go write to your friend for next step.)
e-05.s.s1.hint.0: Look for apology or request for each message.
e-05.s.s1.hint.1: Compare dem by imagining how teacher go feel when she receive each one.
e-05.s.s1.r.b: The reason and situation clear, but without apology or request, e fit sound like you just dey announce am to teacher.
e-05.s.s1.r.c: E give reason but e sound like e dey push blame away, wey fit vex the other person.
e-05.s.s1.r.d: The tone friendly but still polite. The grammar correct too.
e-05.s.s1.explain: a and d get apology, reason, and request. a more formal, d lighter, but both polite. b clear and respectful, but without apology or request e fit sound less polite. For c, pushing blame away fit make other person uncomfortable. The level of formality wey dem expect differ by school and teacher.
e-05.s.s1.acc.0: If you and teacher close, friendly and polite tone like d fit too. a na more formal expression.
e-05.s.s1.acc.1: b get clear reason and situation, plus polite title Ms. Han, so e fine as short notice. But without apology or request, e fit sound less polite than a and d.
e-05.s.s2.prompt: Write your own message to Ms. Han. Talk say you no fit come and give reason (dentist appointment), and add polite expression (apology or request).
e-05.s.s2.hint.0: First think wetin you go add if you dey talk to teacher for Korean, then find how to express the meaning for English.
e-05.s.s2.hint.1: Try write am in this order: sentence say you no fit come, sentence for reason, sentence for request.
e-05.s.s2.selfAssess.0: The tone go make teacher vex when she read am? Which word help with that?
e-05.s.s2.selfAssess.2: If you add something you want (like getting the materials), e sound like request?
e-05.s.s3.prompt: Now na text to friend for same club. Write same situation briefly in 18 words or less, casual tone. (No use formal expressions like Dear or I'm afraid.)
e-05.s.s3.hint.0: Keep only important information from message to teacher (the reason, and say you no fit come).
e-05.s.s3.hint.1: Use contractions (can't) or short words, and count the words.
e-05.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Compare wetin you write to teacher: which words disappear and which remain?
e-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Even though e short, your friend fit understand the reason?
e-05.s.s3.modelNote.1: Friendly tone with apology and question.

e-06.title: Find sentences with schedule overlap inside group message
e-06.goal: Find two schedule sentences for group message wey no match, explain confusion wey dem fit cause, and rewrite dem.
e-06.material: Na message wey leader of science group project post for group chat. (Each line get number. Afternoon time dey written as p.m.)
e-06.thinking.1: Predict the problem wey go happen.
e-06.prereq.0: by / before / after + day or time
e-06.s.s1.prompt: Choose one sentence wey fit cause problem for group members wey follow schedule. Na the line wey time order no match another line.
e-06.s.s1.hint.0: Find all lines wey get time and arrange times in order.
e-06.s.s1.hint.1: Which one come first: deadline to send or time to put together?
e-06.s.s1.explain: The time to put together na Thursday 4:30 p.m., but deadline for parts na Thursday 9:00 p.m. Deadline come after putting together time, so the two lines (line 2 and line 3) conflict. Lines 1 and 4 concern Friday deadline and printing, so dem no conflict.
e-06.s.s2.prompt: Wetin go really happen if people follow this message as e be?
e-06.s.s2.hint.0: Assume one group member send their part exactly “Thursday night.”
e-06.s.s2.hint.1: Wetin leader don finish by that time?
e-06.s.s2.o.a: A part wey due by 9 fit never arrive when dem dey put the parts together by 4:30.
e-06.s.s2.o.b: All the parts go arrive before the work to put dem together, so poster go finish early.
e-06.s.s2.r.b: The putting-together work na 4:30 p.m., and dem dey accept parts till 9:00 p.m. Compare the times again.
e-06.s.s2.o.c: No time remain to print before class on Friday.
e-06.s.s2.r.c: The problem na the order inside Thursday. Time still dey till Friday morning.
e-06.s.s2.explain: Dem go put things together first, but dem still dey accept parts till later, so late part fit no enter.
e-06.s.s3.prompt: Rewrite one of the conflicting lines (or both) in English. Make the days and times match.
e-06.s.s3.hint.0: First decide which of the two lines' times to change.
e-06.s.s3.hint.1: After you change am, read again to check time order “parts deadline → putting together → printing” correct.
e-06.s.s3.placeholder: Example: Please send me your part by ...
e-06.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Deadline to receive parts come before the putting-together time? Compare the two times as numbers.
e-06.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Time still remain before Friday morning deadline?
e-06.s.s3.modelNote.0: I move the parts deadline earlier.
e-06.s.s3.modelNote.1: I move the putting-together time later and add reason.

e-07.title: Combine two notices to work out bus departure time
e-07.goal: Combine two notices posted on different dates (the original time and later change) to work out new departure time, and correct friend misunderstanding with evidence.
e-07.material:
Two notices dey for noticeboard at bus stop. (Only words dem use.)

Notice A (posted on Monday): “Bus 5 leaves at 7:40 a.m.”
Notice B (posted on Wednesday): “From Thursday, Bus 5 will leave 10 minutes earlier. Please be at the stop on time.”

Your friend Hana: “Bus 5 leaves at 7:50 on Thursday.”
Your friend Jae: “Then on Friday it leaves at the same time as on Thursday.”
e-07.thinking.0: Combine different information to reach conclusion.
e-07.thinking.1: Understand how later notice change earlier one.
e-07.prereq.0: Expressions like earlier / later / from + day
e-07.prereq.1: Read time and calculate with time.
e-07.s.s1.prompt: From the two notices, Hana dey correct?
e-07.s.s1.hint.0: Compare the dates wey dem post the two notices. Which one later?
e-07.s.s1.hint.1: Check whether earlier mean “sooner” or “later,” then calculate from 7:40.
e-07.s.s1.o.a: She dey correct. Add B's 10 minutes to A's 7:40, you get 7:50.
e-07.s.s1.r.a: Maybe you read earlier as if e mean later. Check the meaning of earlier again.
e-07.s.s1.o.b: She no dey correct. B talk say e go leave 10 minutes earlier, so na 7:30.
e-07.s.s1.o.c: We no fit tell. We no fit decide which of the notices correct.
e-07.s.s1.r.c: The two notices no contradict. B na later notice wey change A time.
e-07.s.s1.explain: Notice B post later and talk say 10 minutes earlier than A time. 10 minutes before 7:40 na 7:30.
e-07.s.s2.prompt: Jae talk, “On Friday na the same time as Thursday.” How you fit judge this statement from the notices?
e-07.s.s2.hint.0: Try replace “on Thursday” with “from Thursday” and compare whether the meaning change.
e-07.s.s2.hint.1: Look for words for notice wey tell you when e end.
e-07.s.s2.o.a: “From Thursday” mean say e dey continue from Thursday, so Friday time na the same as Thursday.
e-07.s.s2.o.b: “From Thursday” mean say na Thursday alone the change happen.
e-07.s.s2.r.b: “From Thursday” and “on Thursday” different. “From” point to starting time.
e-07.s.s2.o.c: Friday no dey directly for notice, so you fit think say you need check.
e-07.s.s2.r.c: E reasonable to dey careful. But “From Thursday” already include the days after am.
e-07.s.s2.explain: “From Thursday” mean new time start on Thursday. If no word talk when e go end, Friday time na the same. E reasonable too to ask staff because Friday no dey written directly.
e-07.s.s2.acc.0: E reasonable to ask staff because Friday no dey written directly. But “From Thursday” normally mean say e continue after that.
e-07.s.s3.prompt: Reply Hana for English. Talk the bus time for Thursday and give reason from the notices.
e-07.s.s3.hint.0: Start from Notice A time, then write how Notice B change am.
e-07.s.s3.hint.1: Add one sentence to explain “why 7:50 wrong.”
e-07.s.s3.placeholder: Example: I think it leaves at ... because ...
e-07.s.s3.selfAssess.0: E clear which notice you use as evidence?
e-07.s.s3.modelNote.1: Short answer wey argue from meaning of one word.

e-08.title: Write club notice wey no confuse people
e-08.goal: Explain why unclear notice dey confusing, then rewrite the same content for English so anybody wey read am no misunderstand.
e-08.material:
Na notice wey dem put for noticeboard.

“Art Club meeting this Friday or next week at 3 or 4 in room 2 or the gym. Bring something.”

Friends wey read this notice go different places and no meet.
e-08.thinking.0: Find expressions wey get more than one meaning.
e-08.prereq.0: Expressions for day, time, and place.
e-08.s.s1.prompt: Choose all the things wey confuse the friends.
e-08.s.s1.hint.0: Mark the parts of notice wey get “or,” and parts with vague words wey meaning no clear (like something).
e-08.s.s1.hint.1: Check each part whether reader fit understand only one thing and act on am.
e-08.s.s1.r.a: Na true say date no clear. Check whether other items let reader choose just one action too.
e-08.s.s1.r.b: Na true say time no clear. Check whether other items let reader choose just one action too.
e-08.s.s1.r.c: Na true say place no clear. Check whether other items let reader choose just one action too.
e-08.s.s1.r.d: Na true say wetin to bring no clear. Check whether other items let reader choose just one action too.
e-08.s.s1.r.e: E clear which club meeting e be. Choose only parts wey reader fit understand in two or more ways.
e-08.s.s1.explain: Date, time, and place all unclear because of “or,” and wetin to bring unclear because you no know wetin “something” mean. If you choose only some, test whether reader fit act on just one option for the parts wey you leave out.
e-08.s.s2.prompt: Rewrite the notice for the same meeting in English without any misunderstanding. Decide and write the day, time, place, and wetin to bring.
e-08.s.s2.hint.0: For your head, make table and choose one thing each for day, time, place, and wetin to bring.
e-08.s.s2.hint.1: Imagine whether friend wey never go the meeting fit find am with only this notice.
e-08.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Your notice get any part wey give two options with “or”? (For example, two times or two places.)
e-08.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Even friend wey see am for first time fit know where to go?
e-08.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Di date (day) and time both set to one thing each?
e-08.s.s2.modelNote.1: Friendly tone. Di ‘or’ about wetin to bring just give choice; e no confuse.

e-11.title: Check di claim ‘Scores drop, so na Wi-Fi fault’
e-11.goal: Judge whether cause-and-effect reasoning for school newspaper letter enough, decide wetin information people need to check di claim, and politely write counterargument to di writer for English.
e-11.material:
Letter from reader for school newspaper (imaginary text):

‘Last year, our school's average English score was 78. This year, after the school started free Wi-Fi, it fell to 72. So the Wi-Fi caused the drop. Therefore we should turn the Wi-Fi off.’
e-11.thinking.0: Find where argument jump too far
e-11.thinking.1: Choose information wey people need to check am
e-11.prereq.0: Cause-and-effect expressions like therefore / so / caused
e-11.prereq.1: Disagree politely (I see your point, however ...)
e-11.s.s1.prompt: Choose one sentence for this text wey talk like confirmed fact even though proof no enough.
e-11.s.s1.hint.0: Sort each line into ‘something wey happen’ or ‘claim about cause or wetin people suppose do.’
e-11.s.s1.hint.1: Check whether di claim lines follow from fact lines before dem, by dem alone.
e-11.s.s1.explain: Line 3 (‘So the Wi-Fi caused the drop.’) jump from ‘e happen afterward’ to ‘na di cause.’ Di ‘we should turn it off’ for line 4 also no get proof, but e depend on di jump for line 3. Lines 1 and 2 na fact statements about scores and time.
e-11.s.s2.prompt: Wetin information go help you check ‘Wi-Fi na di reason scores drop’? Choose all wey fit help.
e-11.s.s2.hint.0: Think of two reasons apart from Wi-Fi wey fit make scores change.
e-11.s.s2.hint.1: Judge whether each choice fit help tell whether Wi-Fi or another reason cause am.
e-11.s.s2.o.a: How English scores change that year for another school wey no get Wi-Fi
e-11.s.s2.r.a: Comparison na good method. Also check whether you fit find differences in test difficulty or student group.
e-11.s.s2.o.b: Whether this year English test harder pass last year own
e-11.s.s2.r.b: If test change, na important reason. Also compare with other schools and check di student group.
e-11.s.s2.o.c: How many students like English class
e-11.s.s2.r.c: How much students like class fit relate to scores, but e no fit show whether Wi-Fi cause am.
e-11.s.s2.o.d: How much dem pay to install Wi-Fi
e-11.s.s2.r.d: Di cost relate to decision to install am, but e no get anything to do with why scores drop.
e-11.s.s2.o.e: Whether students really use their phones during English class
e-11.s.s2.r.e: This information check di process. Also check other possible reasons (di test, student group, other schools).
e-11.s.s2.o.f: Whether this year students na different group from last year students (skills, how much dem study, etc.)
e-11.s.s2.explain: Compare with other schools (a), check test difficulty (b), check whether dem really use am during class (e), and differences in student group (f) fit help tell whether Wi-Fi or another reason cause di drop. Number of students wey like class and installation cost no relate directly to di cause.
e-11.s.s2.acc.0: Comparing with other schools and checking test difficulty alone don already help check other reasons.
e-11.s.s2.acc.1: If you also check whether dem really use am during class, you fit see di way Wi-Fi might have affected things.
e-11.s.s2.acc.2: Differences in student group na another common reason why scores fit change.
e-11.s.s3.prompt: Write 2-3 sentence counterargument to di writer for English. Accept say scores drop, but explain say proof no yet enough to claim Wi-Fi cause am, and give one way to check or another possible reason.
e-11.s.s3.hint.0: First, acknowledge di part wey di writer get right (scores drop) in one sentence.
e-11.s.s3.hint.1: Then write one clear reason why e no enough to call am ‘di cause’ (which other reason or comparison).
e-11.s.s3.placeholder: Example: I see your point, but ...
e-11.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Your writing accept di fact say scores drop?
e-11.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You give one reason why e no enough to strongly claim say na ‘di cause’?
e-11.s.s3.selfAssess.2: Di tone point out di logic without attacking di writer?

e-12.title: When ‘It's fine.’ no really mean fine: make dialogue
e-12.goal: Judge say words like ‘It's fine.’ fit mean something different from wetin dem literally talk, then create short English dialogue about that kind situation to meet di conditions.
e-12.material: A tell B, ‘I'm sorry I forgot to call you last night.’ B fit answer in different ways. (Na words only.)
e-12.thinking.0: Guess hidden intention from tone and context
e-12.thinking.1: Create dialogue wey meet di conditions
e-12.prereq.1: Expressions like Are you sure? / You sound ...
e-12.s.s1.prompt: Among B answers, which one most likely dey pretend to be fine when e no really fine?
e-12.s.s1.hint.0: Read each answer out loud, and think whether person wey really dey fine go talk that way.
e-12.s.s1.hint.1: Compare whether each answer include ‘reason why e fine’ or ‘something e want,’ or whether dem miss.
e-12.s.s1.r.a: E talk casually and give reason. Di sentence explain why e fine.
e-12.s.s1.r.c: E fit sound awkward because e talk am too strongly, but e hard to judge how person feel from sentence alone.
e-12.s.s1.r.d: E talk say e fine, but e also say wetin e want. E hide less.
e-12.s.s1.explain: If person just talk short, flat ‘It's fine,’ e no show any reason or feeling, so people fit easily think say e dey hide im real feeling. But you no fit know for sure from di sentence alone; check tone and context together.
e-12.s.s1.acc.0: If person stress ‘totally’ too much, e fit mean say dem dey cover up that dem no fine.
e-12.s.s1.acc.1: When person pause for ‘Just...,’ e fit show say dem no completely fine. But e less likely, because dem dey share part of how dem feel.
e-12.s.s2.prompt:
Create English dialogue wey meet these conditions. Start every line with A: or B:, and write at least 4 lines.
Condition 1) B talk say e fine with words like ‘fine’ or ‘okay,’ but e really seem upset.
Condition 2) A notice this and ask gently (use question mark).
Condition 3) At di end, B share small part of how e really feel.
e-12.s.s2.hint.0: First choose one situation (forgot promise, gift, test result, etc.).
e-12.s.s2.hint.1: Make B first answer short, and make A question brief, like ‘Are you sure?’
e-12.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You fit feel from di dialogue say B words (‘fine’) and B real feeling different? Which line show am?
e-12.s.s2.selfAssess.1: A question gentle, no be blame?
e-12.s.s2.selfAssess.2: For di last line, B share small part of how e really feel?
e-12.s.s2.modelNote.0: A flow wey show real feeling in apology situation.
e-12.s.s2.modelNote.1: Dialogue wey meet same conditions with different situation.
